title: Icon & Brand Asset Contract

icon_ref.description: Opaque `iconref:` handle that identifies the asset inside the host registry.
icon_ref.claim_boundary: The reference is opaque and is redacted in diagnostics and serialized audit output.

source.description: Where the bytes come from: `bundled` or `remoteUrl`. Inline data URIs and unknown sources are refused outright.
source.claim_boundary: A remote source must be TLS and must carry an integrity digest; inline payloads are never accepted.

permission.description: The connector's declared right to ship this asset. Only `allowed` is usable; `restricted`, `denied`, and `unknown` are refused.
permission.claim_boundary: Permission is deny-by-default; the host does not infer a right from the presence of a file.

version.description: A semantic version core (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`) that lets the host pin and migrate an asset deterministically.
version.claim_boundary: Floating labels such as `latest`, prefixed versions, and partial versions are refused.

light.description: The light-theme variant: a safe relative bundled path, an https URL, or a registry handle, plus an optional integrity digest.
light.claim_boundary: Path traversal, absolute paths, backslashes, and unsupported extensions are refused rather than normalized.

dark.description: The dark-theme variant, validated exactly like the light variant.
dark.claim_boundary: Both themes are mandatory: an asset without a dark variant is refused rather than silently reused.

fallback.description: What the host renders when the asset cannot be loaded: the host default or a declared fallback reference.
fallback.claim_boundary: `none` is refused, so a failed load can never leave an empty slot.

accessible_name.description: The human-readable name announced by assistive technology. Plain text, non-empty, and bounded.
accessible_name.claim_boundary: Markup, an over-long name, or a raw reference masquerading as a name is refused.

claim_boundary: This is a local icon and brand asset contract, not an image pipeline.
No asset byte, inline payload, or provider credential is stored, returned, or logged.
Icon rasterization, remote fetching, caching, and live brand clearance remain DEFERRED-EXTERNAL.
